motivation: The authors aim to establish exact global optimality and uniqueness for seven-particle cluster configurations in two distinct physical models, strengthening prior numerical or tolerance-based results.
method: They introduce a weak-interaction graph based on pair-geometry thresholds to organize configuration space, combined with graph classification, subset bounds, force balance, geometric certificates, and coercivity/localization arguments.
result: The pentagonal bipyramid is shown to be the unique global energy minimizer for both the seven-particle Lennard-Jones cluster and the seven-charge Thomson problem on a sphere, up to rigid symmetries and relabeling.
conclusion: A common fivefold geometric organizing principle for seven-particle clusters emerges across two very different interaction models, independent of the specific potential.

title: Adaptive Wavefront Shaping Through Flexible Multicore Photonic Lantern Fibres
authors: Robert J. Kilpatrick, Alasdair Milne, Kerrianne Harrington, Thomas A. Wright, Jos\'e C. A. Rocha, Aur\'elien Beno\^it, Helen Parker, Chaitanya K. Mididoddi, James M. Stone, Tim A. Birks, Robert R. Thomson, David B. Phillips
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Holographic micro-endoscopy enables images to be funnelled all-optically through hair-thin strands of optical fibre. Future applications of this technology encompass biomedical imaging within mobile organisms, LiDAR, and industrial inspection. Yet holographic imaging through dynamically flexible optical fibres, called for in many real-world scenarios, represents an ongoing challenge. In this work we demonstrate how a bespoke fibre architecture that we term a 'photonic lantern fibre' offers a way forward. This device benefits from the negligible modal cross-talk of a polarisation-maintaining multicore fibre throughout the majority of its length. A tapered region at one end - known as a photonic lantern - guides light to a short segment of multimode optical fibre. We show how this fibre enables the projection of high-fidelity structured light to the multimode distal fibre facet via wavefront shaping, providing a level of optical control beyond that possible using conventional multicore fibres which suffer from aliasing due to their spatially separated cores. Furthermore, we demonstrate how high-contrast distal focussing can be re-established, anywhere across the output facet, after the multicore fibre is arbitrarily contorted, without access to the distal end. To achieve this we introduce two in-situ bend compensation strategies, that rely on a distally mounted guide-star or analysis of light reflected from the distal facet - offering the future potential for rapid single-shot bend calibration. Our work paves a new route towards the controlled delivery of high-dimensional structured light fields through dynamically flexible optical fibres.
tldr: The paper demonstrates adaptive wavefront shaping through flexible multicore photonic lantern fibres for high-fidelity structured light delivery and distal focusing in holographic micro-endoscopy.
motivation: Holographic imaging through dynamically flexible optical fibres is challenging because conventional multicore fibres suffer from aliasing and bend-induced distortion, limiting real-world endoscopic and sensing applications.
method: The authors use a polarisation-maintaining multicore fibre with a tapered photonic-lantern region coupled to a short multimode fibre, and introduce two in-situ bend compensation strategies based on a distal guide-star or reflected light analysis.
result: They project high-fidelity structured light onto the multimode distal facet and re-establish high-contrast distal focusing anywhere across the output facet after arbitrary fibre contortion without distal access.
conclusion: Photonic lantern fibres enable controlled delivery of high-dimensional structured light through dynamically flexible fibres, offering a route toward rapid single-shot bend calibration for holographic micro-endoscopy and related applications.

title: Telling Coordination From Coincidence: A No-interaction Twin For Collective Systems
authors: Eric J. Couture
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measures of emergence based on information theory or causal closure ask whether a group variable has a predictable law of its own, but not whether that law was produced by the members' interactions: the centre of mass of non-interacting random walkers passes the standard criterion [MATH]. We introduce the interaction share S, the fraction of the forecast error of a system's no-interaction twin (the same members with every interaction removed) that the real group law eliminates, and a projected estimator with expectation zero without interaction. For Gaussian forecasts, [MATH] is the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence of the real group law from the twin's. S is exactly zero for the centre of mass of linearly coupled walkers, and a machine-checked proof extends this to any pairwise force obeying Newton's third law. Across magnets, oscillators and flocking models it rises from 0 to about 1 where collective order appears. With time-shifted virtual groups and positive controls, it separates real fish schools (0.54-0.91, 17 recordings, two species) from groups that never interacted (-0.10 to 0.07), and it falls to zero when zebrafish are placed in the dark. In 221 mouse brain areas and in US stock markets the shares are small (about 1-3%) and were confirmed in pre-registered tests on unseen data. For linear forecasts the share is a memory gap, computable from two autocorrelation curves without fitting a twin; it matches measured shares (Spearman 0.97) and predicted fresh markets within 0.004. All code, data pipelines and hashed pre-registrations are public.
tldr: The paper introduces an information-theoretic 'interaction share' measure that distinguishes genuine interactions in collective systems from coincidental group-level predictability.
motivation: Standard emergence and causal-closure measures can be fooled by non-interacting components whose aggregate variable appears to have its own predictable law, such as the center of mass of independent random walkers.
method: The authors define the interaction share S as the fraction of forecast error eliminated by the real group law relative to a no-interaction twin, with a projected estimator that has zero expectation without interactions and Gaussian/KL-divergence interpretations.
result: S is zero for linearly coupled walkers and pairwise forces obeying Newton's third law, rises with collective order in magnets, oscillators, and flocking models, separates real fish schools from virtual non-interacting groups, and is small in mouse brain and stock-market data.
conclusion: The interaction share provides a principled empirical test for whether collective predictability comes from member interactions rather than coincidence, with public code and pre-registered validations.

title: Coupled Plasmonic Fabry-Perot Resonances Modulating Electromagnetic Enhancement At A Silver Nanowire-nanoparticle Junction Proved By Surface-enhanced Fluorescence Spectroscopy
authors: Yuko S. Yamamoto Tamitake Itoh
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigated the surface-enhanced fluorescence (SEF), which is the broad background spectrum underlying the surface-enhanced resonant Raman scattering of dye molecules, emitted from junctions between silver nanoparticles (NPs) and nanowires (NWs). We found that the electromagnetic enhancement factors (FR) derived from the SEF exhibited spectral modulation, such as complicated oscillatory structures. This property became clearer when the emission polarization was perpendicular to the long axis of the NWs. The FR spectra of the long and short NWs exhibit fine and broad oscillatory structures, respectively, when the NPs are positioned near the NW centers. When the NPs were near the NW ends, a combination of fine and broad structures was observed. Numerical calculations of the position-dependent FR spectra successfully reproduced these properties, indicating that the spectral properties originated from the interaction between two plasmonic Fabry-Perot (FP) resonators within the NW, separated by a NP. Based on this result, an analytical model of coupled FP resonators was developed to evaluate these spectral features using experimentally measured NW lengths and NP positions while varying the inter-resonator coupling efficiency. This analysis revealed that the interference and superposition of the two FP resonances resulted in these complex spectra, the energy of which was radiated by the localized plasmons of the NPs.
tldr: The paper studies spectral modulation of surface-enhanced fluorescence at silver nanoparticle-nanowire junctions and attributes it to coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the origin of broad background SEF spectra underlying surface-enhanced resonant Raman scattering from metal nanostructure junctions.
method: They measure polarization-resolved SEF enhancement spectra for nanoparticles positioned at different locations along silver nanowires and compare them with numerical calculations and an analytical coupled-Fabry-Perot-resonator model.
result: The enhancement spectra show fine or broad oscillatory structures depending on nanowire length and nanoparticle position, reproduced by coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances whose interference and superposition shape the complex spectra.
conclusion: The work provides an analytical picture of how coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot modes modulate electromagnetic enhancement at nanowire-nanoparticle junctions, with localized nanoparticle plasmons radiating the coupled resonance energy.

title: Dynamic Scaling And Aging In Hydrodynamic Coarsening Of Vapor Bubbles In A Lennard-Jones Fluid
authors: Sutapa Roy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the coarsening and aging dynamics of vapor bubbles during liquid-vapor phase separation in a three-dimensional single-component Lennard-Jones fluid using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Following a temperature quench from a homogeneous high-temperature state into the two-phase coexistence region, vapor bubbles nucleate and grow in the liquid background. The characteristic bubble size follows a power-law growth, [MATH], with a growth exponent [MATH], characteristic of inertial hydrodynamic coarsening. We also investigate the two-time autocorrelation function [MATH] which follows waiting-time dependent relaxation, revealing aging. Furthermore, data at different waiting times collapse onto a scaling function when plotted as a function of the length ratio [MATH], demonstrating dynamical scaling during aging. The corresponding scaling function exhibits an algebraic decay with an exponent [MATH]. Interestingly, bubble and droplet growth exhibit distinctly different domain-growth and aging exponents despite both being disconnected morphologies.
tldr: This paper studies coarsening and aging dynamics of vapor bubbles during liquid-vapor phase separation in a classical Lennard-Jones fluid using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: The work aims to characterize dynamic scaling and aging in hydrodynamic domain growth for vapor bubbles, contrasting bubble and droplet morphologies.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of a three-dimensional single-component Lennard-Jones fluid are used after a temperature quench into the two-phase coexistence region.
result: Bubble size grows as a power law with an inertial hydrodynamic exponent, and the two-time autocorrelation function shows waiting-time-dependent aging with data collapse onto a scaling function.
conclusion: The study finds distinct domain-growth and aging exponents for bubbles versus droplets, despite both being disconnected morphologies.

title: Nonlinear Optical Properties Of MXenes For Photonic Applications
authors: Alina Karabchevsky, Shadad Watad, Aviad Katiyi, Muhammad Sharif Uddin, Nicol\'as Abad\'ia, Anupma Thakur, Babak Anasori
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MXenes - a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides - have emerged as powerful nonlinear photonic materials owing to their metallic conductivity, ultrafast carrier dynamics, broadband optical response, and highly tunable surface chemistry. This Review provides the first comprehensive overview of the nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of MXenes and their growing impact on advanced photonic technologies. We discuss state-of-the-art synthesis strategies, from fluoride-based etching to molten-salt, electrochemical, and CVD-enabled routes, highlighting how structural quality and surface terminations govern optical behaviour. A detailed analysis of third-order nonlinearities including Kerr effects, two- and multi-photon absorption, saturable and reverse-saturable absorption, and harmonic generation is presented, supported by quantitative comparisons across MXene families. We further examine modelling approaches linking band structure to nonlinear response and survey application frontiers such as gas sensing, ultrafast lasers, all-optical limiters, and emerging photonic neural networks. Finally, we outline future research directions spanning material engineering, device integration, and quantum/nonlinear metasurface platforms. Together, these insights position MXenes as a transformative materials platform for next-generation nonlinear photonics and ultrafast all-optical information processing.
tldr: This review surveys the nonlinear optical properties of MXene materials and their applications in photonics.
motivation: MXenes are emerging 2D materials with tunable optical response and ultrafast carrier dynamics, motivating a comprehensive overview of their nonlinear photonic potential.
method: The authors review synthesis routes, third-order nonlinear optical effects, modeling approaches, and application frontiers for MXenes.
result: The review compiles quantitative comparisons of Kerr effects, multi-photon absorption, saturable absorption, and harmonic generation across MXene families, and surveys uses in sensing, lasers, limiters, and photonic neural networks.
conclusion: MXenes are positioned as promising materials for next-generation nonlinear photonics and all-optical information processing, with future directions in material engineering and device integration.

title: Improving The Convergence Of Coupled Quasinormal-mode Theory For Optical Resonators
authors: Tong Wu, Philippe Lalanne, Haitao Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) provide a rigorous framework for describing resonances in open optical systems, including radiative and material losses. Recent coupled-QNM theories use the modes of individual resonators to predict the resonances and optical responses of coupled systems, without relying on phenomenological coupling parameters. However, their accuracy can deteriorate when the resonators confine light weakly and radiate strongly, often requiring many modes to obtain reliable predictions. Here, we introduce a reformulation of coupled-QNM theory that substantially improves its accuracy when only a small number of modes of the individual resonators are retained. The approach builds on the same underlying QNM framework but treats the fields mediating the interaction between resonators differently, leading to a new expression for the coupling coefficients. Numerical comparisons show that this extended-domain formulation is particularly advantageous for resonators with strong ra-diative losses, enabling more efficient modeling of a broader range of coupled photonic sys-tems.
tldr: A reformulation of coupled quasinormal-mode theory that improves accuracy when only few modes of individual optical resonators are retained, particularly for strongly radiating resonators.
motivation: Existing coupled-QNM approaches lose accuracy for weakly confining, strongly radiating resonators and require many modes, so a more efficient modal expansion is needed for modeling coupled photonic systems.
method: The authors keep the QNM framework but treat the interaction-mediating fields over an extended domain, deriving a new expression for the coupling coefficients, and benchmark against numerical full-wave results.
result: The extended-domain formulation converges much faster with mode number than standard coupled-QNM theory, with the largest gains for resonators with strong radiative losses.
conclusion: The improved scheme enables efficient, accurate modeling of a broader class of coupled optical resonators without phenomenological coupling parameters.

title: Excluding 54 Of The 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns Of The Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
authors: Valery Asiryan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be Sharipov's even monic degree-[MATH] third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over [MATH]. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by [MATH]. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over [MATH], using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from [MATH]. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly [MATH] of the [MATH] nontrivial partitions of [MATH], thereby excluding [MATH] complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, [MATH] follow from evenness alone and [MATH] from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.
tldr: The paper establishes a uniform normal form for the complete factorization of Sharipov's even monic degree-12 cuboid polynomial over the rationals, excluding 54 of the 76 nontrivial irreducible degree patterns.
motivation: Understanding the factorization structure of the cuboid polynomial bears on the perfect cuboid problem, and a systematic classification of possible irreducible degree patterns is needed to constrain the search for rational factorizations.
method: The authors combine Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction over the rationals to derive a normal form built from even quadratic factors, higher-degree even irreducible factors, and symmetry-exchanged factor pairs, subject to degree, sign, and obligatory-factor constraints; an exact verification script accompanies the proofs.
result: The normal form leaves exactly 22 of the 76 nontrivial partitions of the degree, excluding 54 patterns, of which some follow from evenness alone and the rest from the arithmetic restrictions on rational factor constants via prime valuations and a real-root argument on an auxiliary sextic.
conclusion: The eliminated patterns are proven impossible, but the remaining patterns are only necessary possibilities, so full irreducibility of the cuboid polynomial remains open.

title: Analytic Criteria For Criticality Of Subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger Operators
authors: Takumu Ooi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schr\"{o}dinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator.
tldr: The paper introduces an analogue of the bottom of the spectrum for subordinated Schrödinger operators and derives analytic criteria classifying them as subcritical, critical, or supercritical.
motivation: Criticality theory for Schrödinger operators is well developed, but analogous analytic criteria for subordinated Schrödinger operators are less understood and require separate treatment.
method: The author defines a quantity playing the role of the spectral bottom for subordinated Schrödinger operators and uses analytic techniques to characterize subcriticality, criticality, and supercriticality.
result: Analytic criteria are established that distinguish subcritical, critical, and supercritical subordinated Schrödinger operators.
conclusion: The work extends criticality theory to subordinated Schrödinger operators and provides practical analytic conditions for classifying their critical behavior.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Systems Beyond Joules: A Review Of Unexpected Application Domains
authors: Mauricio Mu\~noz-Arias
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. Over the past fifteen years it has spread to chemistry, cell biology, fusion plasmas, musical instruments, district heating, electricity markets, macroeconomics, predator-prey ecology, optimization algorithms and neural-network training. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.
tldr: A review mapping port-Hamiltonian systems theory beyond mechanical and electrical domains into chemistry, biology, economics, ecology, optimization, and machine learning.
motivation: The port-Hamiltonian framework was originally designed for physical systems with stored energy and power ports, but it has recently been applied in many unexpected domains; the paper aims to survey and classify this spread.
method: The author reviews checked literature and classifies each application by whether its Hamiltonian represents physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function without energetic meaning.
result: The review finds a continuum: applications with genuine thermodynamic potentials are deep and constructive, while borrowed-energy applications still benefit from compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities but are younger and more scattered.
conclusion: The paper closes with speculative research directions, including port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics, supply chains, and learned digital twins for structural health monitoring.

title: Testing CCZ-equivalence To Permutations Via Projections Of Walsh Zero Spaces, With Applications To Apn Functions
authors: Emanuele Bellini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension [MATH] is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary [MATH]-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in [MATH]. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to [MATH] and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of [MATH] and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them [MATH] to [MATH] times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions [MATH], which G\"ololu and Pavl proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when [MATH] divides [MATH]. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even [MATH]. In dimension [MATH] the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile [MATH] classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.
tldr: The paper develops an exact algorithmic test for CCZ-equivalence of APN functions to permutations using projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to quadratic APN functions in even dimensions.
motivation: The existence of APN permutations in even dimension is a long-standing open problem, and testing whether known APN functions are CCZ-equivalent to permutations is a natural approach toward it.
method: The authors reconstruct complementary n-dimensional subspaces from their projections to an n-dimensional space, reducing the problem to searches for subspaces and constrained bilinear maps, and implement a faster test than generic sboxU searches.
result: The test is orders of magnitude faster on dimension-twelve benchmarks, shows that certain Gölolu–Pavlu functions are not CCZ-equivalent to permutations for every even n, and compiles ten-dimensional quadratic APN classes with no CCZ-equivalence to permutations.
conclusion: The work provides an efficient exact test for CCZ-equivalence to permutations for APN functions with affine Walsh supports and supports a conjecture that a family of APN functions is never CCZ-equivalent to permutations in even dimension.

title: The Power Of Two Choices In Dynamic Pricing: As Good As Full Feedback, Instance-Wise
authors: Yan Dai, Tao Lin, Aleksandrs Slivkins
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamic pricing problem, where a firm sells a product to [MATH] myopic customers and their values are independent samples from an unknown value distribution [MATH]. With posted prices, the firm only sees whether each customer buys, and the minimax regret is [MATH] [KL03]. A menu instead offers several options, each selling the product with some probability at some expected payment. Infinitely many menu options allow the seller to fully reveal customer values, reducing the regret to [MATH]. How many options are needed? Perhaps surprisingly, a second menu option suffices, achieving the same regret as infinite menus (up to [MATH] factors). This holds broadly: without knowing any property of [MATH], our algorithm with two menu options attains [MATH] regret in general, [MATH] regret for monotone-hazard-rate distributions, and [MATH] instance-dependent regret when [MATH] is a suitable notion of "dimension". All are optimal even with infinite menus. Moreover, we argue, via a novel lower-bound construction, that our algorithm is near-optimal for each problem instance. Along the way, we study the query complexity of revenue maximization, where an algorithm issues a query to each customer to learn the property of interest (either the best price or the CDF) up to some precision. We show that interval queries suffice to achieve the same query complexity as value queries (up to [MATH] factors) for both properties and across several classes of value distributions. We provide a new interval-query algorithm for each property. The best-price-estimation algorithm is the key ingredient in our main dynamic pricing algorithm, and the CDF-estimation algorithm underpins a simpler algorithm attaining [MATH] regret with three menu options.
tldr: A classical online-learning theory paper showing that a two-option menu suffices to match the instance-wise regret of infinitely many menu options in dynamic pricing with myopic customers.
motivation: Posted-price mechanisms only reveal purchase decisions, yielding Theta(sqrt(T)) minimax regret, while rich menus can nearly fully reveal buyer valuations; the paper asks how many menu options are actually needed to capture this benefit.
method: The authors design an interval-query-based best-price-estimation subroutine and build a dynamic pricing algorithm using only two menu options, complemented by a novel instance-wise lower-bound construction and a study of query complexity for revenue maximization and CDF estimation.
result: Two menu options achieve the same regret as infinite menus up to logarithmic factors: general, monotone-hazard-rate, and instance-dependent bounds that are optimal even with infinitely many options, and the algorithm is shown near-optimal per instance.
conclusion: A minimal two-option menu is essentially as powerful as full value feedback for dynamic pricing, and interval queries are as powerful as value queries for the estimation tasks studied.

title: Beyond Node Strengths: The Topological Content Of Weighted Bipartite Networks
authors: Daniele Cirulli, Lorenzo Buffa, Giulio Cimini, Dario Mazzilli, Aurelio Patelli, Fabio Saracco
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.
tldr: The paper introduces a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks to determine whether node strengths alone explain observed topology or additional structural information is present.
motivation: Weighted bipartite networks encode both interaction topology and intensity, but it is often unclear whether simple node-strength constraints suffice to reproduce empirical network structure.
method: The authors construct maximum-entropy models preserving node strengths alone, strengths plus global density, and strengths plus the full degree sequence, and apply them across economic, technological, ecological, social, and lexical systems with a scalable computational workflow.
result: Strength constraints alone are generally insufficient, but the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single density constraint often suffices, while stronger residual degree heterogeneity requires node-specific constraints.
conclusion: Topology is essential but often compressible in statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and the choice of topological resolution affects which interactions and projected relationships are statistically significant.

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation And Interface Passivation In Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Ying Tang, Zuhong Zhang, Hongzhuo Wu, Zhihao Li, Zhenhuang Su, Yonggang Yang, Hairui Liu, Feng Yang, Zhe Li, Luca Sapienza, Jorge Pascual, Shengnan Zuo, Bo Hou, Antonio Abate, Meng Li, Yufang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn[MATH] coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn[MATH] to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.
tldr: The paper introduces a dynamic molecular transformation strategy using 1-acetylpiperazine to regulate crystallization and passivate interfaces in tin-based perovskite solar cells, achieving 15.18% efficiency and improved stability.
motivation: Tin-based perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic materials but suffer from unstable Sn²⁺ coordination, rapid crystallization, and interfacial defects that limit performance and stability.
method: The authors use 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) during film formation: its carbonyl group coordinates with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursors and control crystal growth, while annealing induces in situ transformation into amidinium-functionalized species that passivate surface A-site vacancies.
result: The coupled bulk-to-interface engineering yields compact, highly crystalline films and devices with 15.18% power conversion efficiency, retaining 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
conclusion: Dynamic molecular transformation offers a route to simultaneously control crystallization and passivate interfaces, advancing efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Geometric Classification Of Noether Invariants Of The Time-Dependent Damped Duffing Oscillator
authors: And Aniekan Magnus Ukpong Michael Tsamparlis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a systematic geometric classification of the Noether point symmetries of time-dependent conformal Lagrangians of the form [MATH], whose Euler--Lagrange equations describe dynamical systems with time-dependent linear damping. The classification is carried out by coupling the temporal parameters of the conformal factor [MATH] with the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric [MATH] through a set of compatibility and integrability conditions. The central result is a main theorem which determines the Noether generators, the associated gauge functions and the resulting invariants. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity [MATH] is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on [MATH], [MATH] or [MATH], and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space [MATH] with [MATH] and potential [MATH]. For the damped harmonic oscillator ([MATH]) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies [MATH]. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.
tldr: A geometric classification of Noether point symmetries and invariants for time-dependent conformal Lagrangians describing linearly damped systems, applied to the damped Duffing oscillator.
motivation: Damped nonlinear oscillators such as the Duffing oscillator generally lack global conservation laws, so the authors seek a systematic, fully covariant framework for deriving Noether invariants for time-dependent dissipative systems.
method: The classification couples the temporal parameters of the conformal factor to the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric via compatibility and integrability conditions, yielding a main theorem that splits into cases depending on a key quantity and on whether homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient.
result: The theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant for the damped harmonic oscillator and yields a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant for the anharmonic case when the linear stiffness satisfies a specific condition, each verified by direct differentiation.
conclusion: The work provides a rare global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, with potential use for the integration and quantization of the damped Duffing oscillator.

title: Linear Response For Self-Consistent Transfer Operators On Graphons
authors: Herbert M. C. Maquera
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon [MATH], as introduced in . We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point [MATH] of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula. Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre [MATH] equals [MATH], where [MATH] is the degree function of the graphon and [MATH] is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with [MATH] edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of [MATH]. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.
tldr: The paper develops a linear response theory for equilibrium states of large heterogeneous networks of weakly coupled expanding circle maps whose thermodynamic limit is described by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator on a graphon.
motivation: Statistical properties of large coupled dynamical networks in the thermodynamic limit are captured by transfer operators on graphons, but how the equilibrium state responds to changes in coupling strength or network topology was not understood.
method: The authors prove differentiability of the attracting fixed point of the Self-Consistent Transfer Operator in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces and derive a linear response formula, with a tree/homomorphism-density expansion of perturbative coefficients.
result: At zero coupling the response factorises: node susceptibility is proportional to the graphon degree function times a universal profile, with finer topology entering only at higher order via rooted homomorphism densities of trees; Green-Kubo expressions and a graphon-perturbation response formula are also obtained.
conclusion: Heterogeneity of linear statistical response in such networks is dictated at leading order by the degree profile alone, with topology visible only at second order and beyond, yielding testable predictions for finite networks.

title: Basis Selection, Universal Sampling Discretization, And Sampling Recovery
authors: Feng Dai, Jiashu Ran, Vladimir N. Temlyakov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every real [MATH]-dimensional subspace of [MATH], we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every [MATH], at most [MATH] positively weighted samples discretize the squared [MATH] norm of all [MATH]-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted [MATH] estimates and a sharp [MATH] bound for the squared [MATH] norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from [MATH] samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.
tldr: The paper constructs orthonormal bases for finite-dimensional subspaces that allow a small number of weighted samples to discretize squared L2 norms of all m-term combinations, and derives sampling recovery estimates.
motivation: Sampling discretization and recovery of functions from finite-dimensional subspaces are central problems in approximation theory and learning theory, where one wants guarantees that hold uniformly over all elements of a prescribed coefficient class.
method: The authors build a single orthonormal basis per subspace via random rotations so that positively weighted point samples discretize the squared L2 norm of every m-term combination, then apply a change of measure under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.
result: They obtain simultaneous weighted L2 estimates, a sharp bound on the squared L2 norm of the pointwise maximum, and sampling recovery error estimates using a prescribed number of samples for given coefficient classes.
conclusion: The work provides universal discretization and recovery guarantees of interest to approximation theory and statistical learning, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, And Weak Mixing For $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
authors: Chunlin Liu, Kairan Liu, Tao Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for [MATH]-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and ahin for [MATH]-actions. We note that in their recent paper , Robinson and ahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for [MATH]-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.
tldr: The paper proves Birkhoff- and von Neumann-type ergodic theorems for Z^2 measure-preserving systems along irrational directions, and characterizes directional ergodicity and weak mixing.
motivation: Ergodic theorems for multiparameter (Z^2) actions along irrational directions lack a complete dynamical treatment, and the equivalence between dynamical and spectral notions of directional ergodicity/weak mixing requires clarification.
method: Pure mathematical analysis of measure-preserving Z^2-actions, establishing directional ergodic and mean ergodic theorems and comparing dynamical definitions with the spectral definitions of Robinson, Rosenblatt and Şahin.
result: Directional Birkhoff and von Neumann theorems are obtained, dynamical and spectral characterizations of directional ergodicity and weak mixing are shown to coincide, via an approach distinct from that of Robinson and Şahin.
conclusion: The framework unifies dynamical and spectral viewpoints on directional ergodicity and weak mixing for Z^2-actions, providing a self-contained alternative proof route.

title: zk-DEAP: A Zero-Knowledge Decentralized Encrypted Aggregation Protocol
authors: Jude Ramanan, Georgiana Haldeman, Noah Apthorpe
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure aggregation in domains such as federated learning, Internet of Things, and voting requires operating on private inputs while preserving confidentiality, verifying that each input satisfies constraints, and avoiding trusted parties. Existing protocols achieve at most two of these requirements. We present zk-DEAP, a protocol combining lifted ElGamal homomorphic encryption, FROST threshold cryptography, and zero-knowledge proofs (Bulletproofs, zk-SNARKs, or zk-STARKs) for fully decentralized, verifiable, privacy-preserving aggregation. Our core technical contribution is a cryptographic binding mechanism preventing substitution attacks, where a valid proof for one input is paired with a ciphertext encrypting a different, malicious value. For Bulletproofs, we bind via ciphertext-derived randomness modification. For zk-SNARKs/zk-STARKs, to bind across algebraic structures (a well-known challenge in practical cryptography), we introduce a novel blinded arithmetic hash commitment with an embedded Schnorr constraint. These binding techniques force the ZKP's private witness to equal the encrypted value, ensuring any circuit-verified constraint applies to the ciphertext. We implement three production-ready, defense-in-depth variants in Rust and evaluate across 5-500 participants. Compared to unverified aggregation, zk-DEAP adds modest overhead while providing cryptographic guarantees against input manipulation that statistical defenses cannot match.
tldr: zk-DEAP is a classical cryptographic protocol for decentralized verifiable encrypted aggregation using homomorphic encryption, threshold signatures, and zero-knowledge proofs.
motivation: Secure aggregation in federated learning, IoT, and voting needs confidentiality, input validation, and no trusted parties, but existing protocols achieve at most two of these simultaneously.
method: The protocol combines lifted ElGamal homomorphic encryption, FROST threshold cryptography, and zero-knowledge proofs with new binding mechanisms that force the ZKP witness to match the encrypted value and prevent ciphertext substitution attacks.
result: The authors implement three Rust variants and evaluate them for 5-500 participants, finding modest overhead compared with unverified aggregation while providing cryptographic input-manipulation guarantees.
conclusion: zk-DEAP provides fully decentralized, verifiable, privacy-preserving aggregation, but it is a classical cryptography and distributed-systems contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Applicative Theories Can Count
authors: Melissa Antonelli, Marcel Ertel, Eduardo Skapinakis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applicative theories offer a proof-theoretic framework for studying complexity. In this paper, we introduce a family of applicative theories to characterize classes ranging from constant-depth circuits to polynomial space. Our approach relies on a simple axiom scheme, the small variations of which allows to capture various forms of counting and alternation. This leads to highly uniform results. When applied on notation, the scheme captures bit counting, yielding a characterization of the functions computable by constant-depth, polynomial-size threshold circuits ([MATH]); when applied lexicographically, it allows for the counting of accepting computations, yielding a characterization of the functions in the counting hierarchy ([MATH]). Increasing the logical complexity of the induction formulas allowed in the scheme, we obtain characterizations of the functions computable by bounded Boolean circuits of logarithmic-depth and polynomial-size ([MATH]) and of the functions computable in polynomial space ([MATH]). The latter characterization solves an open problem in the field. Finally, we investigate separation results. While it is unknown whether [MATH] and [MATH] are different, there is an oracle relative to which (relativized) [MATH] is strictly contained in (relativized) [MATH]. We use this fact to separate the theories characterizing them, by exploring their ability to represent higher-order functionals.
tldr: The paper introduces applicative theories that characterize complexity classes from constant-depth circuits to polynomial space via a uniform axiom scheme for counting and alternation.
motivation: Applicative theories provide a proof-theoretic framework for studying computational complexity, and the authors aim to capture counting and alternation phenomena uniformly across several complexity classes.
method: They define a family of applicative theories based on a simple axiom scheme, varying its application (notation vs. lexicographic) and the logical complexity of induction formulas to characterize different complexity classes.
result: The theories characterize functions computable by constant-depth threshold circuits, the counting hierarchy, bounded logarithmic-depth Boolean circuits, and polynomial space; the latter solves an open problem. Separation results are also obtained using an oracle.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small variations of a single axiom scheme yield highly uniform complexity characterizations and provides new separation techniques for the corresponding theories.

title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid Mimo Systems Employing Circular Arrays
authors: Priya Gupta, Prabhanshu Yadav, Suraj Srivastava
abstract: ArXiv:2611.11097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.
tldr: The paper proposes a QoS-aware, energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing framework for near-field sub-THz multiuser massive MIMO downlink systems using a large uniform circular array at the base station.
motivation: Near-field communications are a candidate enabler for 6G networks, but designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing for multiuser systems is hard because of non-convex QoS constraints and hybrid hardware limitations.
method: A transmit-power minimization problem with QoS constraints is solved via a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) that converts QoS constraints into second-order cone constraints, combined with a near-field polar-domain codebook and an MMV sparse-approximation hybrid precoder design solved by low-complexity SOMP.
result: Simulations show the proposed framework attains spectral and energy efficiency close to ideal fully digital beamfocusing while offering a favorable hardware-complexity/performance trade-off.
conclusion: The hybrid UCA-based near-field architecture with the PDJO-plus-codebook design is an effective and energy-efficient alternative to fully digital beamfocusing for sub-THz multiuser systems.

title: On Transportation Of Constrictions On Phase-lock Areas Of Overdamped Josephson Junction By Means Of Isomonodromic Deformation Of The Associated Special Double Confluent Heun Equation
authors: S. I. Tertychniy
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An example of computation of locations of constrictions on the phase-lock area in the parameter space for the equation modeling dynamics of overdamped Josephson junction is discussed. Several conjectures of qualitative character are inferred from the heuristic data thus obtained. The method applying isomonodromic deformations of the special double confluent Heun equation associated with the noted model is used. Such a deformation is controlled by the data provided by solution to a Third Painlev\`e equation for which a new representation in conjunction with the corresponding non-linear second order differential equation fairly efficient in the treatment of the problem in question is proposed.
tldr: The paper computes the locations of constrictions on phase-lock areas in the parameter space of an overdamped Josephson junction model using isomonodromic deformations of a special double confluent Heun equation.
motivation: Phase-lock areas of the overdamped Josephson junction equation are a mathematically rich object, and their fine structure (constrictions) needs better analytic tools than heuristic numerics.
method: The author applies isomonodromic deformation theory to the special double confluent Heun equation associated with the junction model, controlled by solutions of a third Painleve equation for which a new representation is proposed.
result: Locations of constrictions are computed for an example, and several qualitative conjectures are inferred from the heuristic data.
conclusion: The technique offers an efficient route to describing phase-lock area geometry, but the results remain conjectural and purely mathematical.

title: Persistent A-homotopy Of Complex Networks
authors: Milan Rajkovic
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph [MATH]-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent [MATH]-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial [MATH]-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.
tldr: The paper introduces a persistent A-homotopy construction for complex networks that tracks how loop classes change when short cycles are declared contractible, yielding a computable bridge between persistent A-homotopy and persistent homology.
motivation: The work aims to separate the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations, addressing distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permits.
method: It defines a sequence of quotient groups by declaring cycles up to a prescribed length contractible, obtaining the clique-complex fundamental group at length three and the graph A-fundamental group at length four, with mod-two abelianisation summarized by a barcode whose death scales come from a minimum cycle basis.
result: The construction is illustrated on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks, and nine benchmark networks; filling plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the torus fundamental group, and the barcode death scales distinguish network models and randomizations.
conclusion: The group construction and its linear summary provide computable certificates of non-trivial A-classes and connect persistent A-homotopy to persistent homology in network settings.

title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead Stars As Factories Of The Most Extreme Objects In The Universe
authors: Swagat S. Mishra Ankit C. Khunt
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.
tldr: A pedagogical review of white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes, and primordial black holes as extreme astrophysical objects governed by quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, and general relativity.
motivation: The authors aim to explain how stellar evolution and fundamental physics determine the endpoints of stars and the possible role of primordial black holes in dark matter.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical account rather than new calculations, synthesizing known physics of compact objects and primordial black holes.
result: It describes the formation and properties of white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, and briefly discusses primordial black holes as dark matter candidates.
conclusion: The work is an educational overview of compact astrophysical objects with no direct contribution to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Same Contacts, Different Rooms:Meeting Format Shapes Llm Group Influence Beyond Pairwise Contact Counts
authors: Zhexi Gu, Shusheng Cao, Runping Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulations of LLM agent collectives usually summarise interaction as a pairwise contact network. We test that summary with a contact-matched intervention: the members, their initial stances and every pairwise contact count stay fixed while the meetings are reorganised, and each member gives a one-step support readout after reading the arguments of everyone present. Across six open-weight LLMs and 14 debate topics, merging triads into five-person meetings (resize) moves group support more than reshuffling who meets in triads (regroup), although both move the same 60 dyadic exposures. The root-mean-square change is 4.36 versus 2.59 percentage points (pp), larger for resize in all six models and in 81 of 84 model-topic cells. Resizing also has a consistent direction: it amplifies the initial majority of the merged members by 1.72 pp, in every model, whereas regrouping has no direction (<= 0.03 pp). A contact network cannot represent regrouping at all, yet pairwise rules applied meeting by meeting explain up to 76% of its effect, and with identical weights they raise resize R^2 by 0.51-0.58 for two models. We show that the gap between the two placements is an exact Jensen gap of the sigmoid readout, bounded by how much a member's predicted logits vary across meetings; this dispersion tracks the gap with log-log r=0.97 and tells a modeller when contact counts are a safe summary. Meeting format is a first-class variable for LLM social simulation.
tldr: The paper studies how meeting format affects LLM group influence in agent collectives beyond pairwise contact counts.
motivation: LLM agent simulations often reduce interactions to pairwise contact networks, but this may miss higher-order effects of meeting structure.
method: Using a contact-matched intervention across six open-weight LLMs and 14 debate topics, the authors compare reorganizing triads into five-person meetings versus reshuffling triad membership while keeping dyadic exposures fixed.
result: Resizing meetings moves group support more than regrouping (4.36 vs 2.59 pp RMS change), amplifies initial majorities by 1.72 pp, and the gap is explained as a Jensen gap of the sigmoid readout.
conclusion: Meeting format is a first-class variable for LLM social simulation and contact networks are not always a safe summary of group influence.

title: The Physics Of Interstellar Travel
authors: Coryn A. L. Bailer-Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How can we send an uncrewed spacecraft to the nearest stars within a human lifetime? What propulsion methods are available? Will it survive impacts in the interstellar medium? What science will it do at its destination? How can it send back data over enormous distances? In this short semi-popular article, I examine various aspects of the physics of interstellar travel, its challenges and possible solutions. I focus on nuclear rockets, laser sails, dust impacts, and communication. These, as well as other issues such as navigation and onboard power, are explored in more detail in my book, The Physics of Interstellar Travel (2026).
tldr: A short semi-popular review of the physics of uncrewed interstellar spacecraft, covering propulsion, dust impacts, navigation, power, and communication.
motivation: The article asks how a probe could reach the nearest stars within a human lifetime and survive and operate there, aiming to survey the physical challenges and possible solutions.
method: Qualitative/conceptual physics analysis drawing on known engineering estimates, focusing on nuclear rockets, laser sails, interstellar dust impact hazards, and long-distance communication.
result: The article summarizes feasibility considerations and trade-offs for candidate propulsion and shielding/communication schemes rather than presenting new quantitative results.
conclusion: Interstellar travel is physically conceivable but faces severe engineering constraints; details are deferred to the author's book.

title: Precision-informed Fourier Compression Of Refractive Index Tomograms With Voxel-wise Error Control
authors: Dohyeon Lee, Juheon Lee, Sehyeon Lee, Juyeon Park, Yongkeun Park
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Significance: Holotomography (HT) generates large refractive index (RI) volumes and time series, creating a need for compact storage with controlled numerical fidelity. Aim: We sought to reduce storage by directly encoding reconstructed three-dimensional RI volumes in Fourier space with voxelwise validation against an assigned error budget. Approach: Quantized Fourier coefficients represent volumetric structure, while spatial residual quantization uses a 1% safety margin without storing separate corrections for individual voxels. We evaluated cellular and organoid data, concurrent processing, and extensions to dielectric-tensor and absorption tomography. Results: At a budget of 0.0001 RI units, complete packets achieved compression ratios of 7.89-9.50 relative to float32 arrays and were 28-30% smaller than BitRound-Pcodec packets satisfying the same error limit. Concurrent processing reduced encoding and decoding wall times by factors of 5.14 and 4.81 without changing packets. The fixed margin passed all primary-budget tests but failed at one smaller budget in both precision-sweep inputs. Conclusions: Precision-informed volumetric Fourier coding reduces storage of holotomograms with verified voxel-wise fidelity at the primary budget, at additional computational cost.
tldr: The paper presents a precision-informed Fourier-space compression scheme for three-dimensional refractive index tomograms with voxel-wise error control.
motivation: Holotomography produces large refractive index volumes and time series, creating a need for compact storage that preserves numerical fidelity within an assigned error budget.
method: Reconstructed 3D refractive index volumes are encoded directly in Fourier space using quantized Fourier coefficients, with spatial residual quantization applying a fixed 1% safety margin instead of storing per-voxel corrections.
result: At a budget of 0.0001 RI units, compression ratios of 7.89–9.50 relative to float32 were achieved, 28–30% smaller than BitRound-Pcodec packets at the same error limit, though the fixed margin failed at one smaller budget.
conclusion: Precision-informed volumetric Fourier coding reduces holotomogram storage with verified voxel-wise fidelity at the primary budget, at additional computational cost.

title: Spectroscopic Method For Determining The Onset Of Clustering In Supersonic Gas Jets
authors: Yu. S. Doronin, A. A. Tkachenko, V. L. Vakula, G. V. Kamarchuk
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents an original spectroscopic method for determining the parameters of the initial stage of clustering in supersonic jets. The method was tested on supersonic jets of argon and nitrogen, excited by electrons at a distance of 30 millimetres from the nozzle exit, where the influence of secondary processes on the intensity of the observed radiation is significantly suppressed. For argon, the continuum emission from neutral excited clusters was used as an indicator of cluster formation in the supersonic argon jet. In the case of nitrogen, for which no emissions attributable exclusively to clusters have been recorded, a study was carried out on the effect of clustering on the redistribution of the intensities of atomic lines and molecular bands in the Lyman Birge Hopfield system.
tldr: The paper introduces a spectroscopic technique to detect and characterize the onset of cluster formation in supersonic argon and nitrogen jets excited by electron impact.
motivation: Supersonic gas jets are widely used in beam, plasma and spectroscopy experiments, but determining when clusters begin to form (and how large they are) is difficult; a reliable, non-intrusive diagnostic is needed.
method: Electron-excited emission spectra were recorded 30 mm downstream from the nozzle exit to suppress secondary processes, using neutral cluster continuum emission as a clustering indicator for argon and studying clustering-induced redistribution of atomic lines and Lyman-Birge-Hopfield molecular bands for nitrogen.
result: Clustering onset and the associated emission features in argon and nitrogen jets were identified and characterized, with the method validated on both a clustering-friendly (Ar) and a non-clustering-emission (N2) gas.
conclusion: The spectroscopic approach provides a practical means to determine the initial clustering stage parameters in supersonic jets, though it is a gas-dynamics/atomic-physics diagnostic with no quantum information content.

title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions In Generalized Metric Spaces With Weighted Graphs
authors: Muhammad Aslam Javed Ismat Beg
abstract: ArXiv:2611.09996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.
tldr: The paper introduces graded-edge Rakotch contractions on generalized metric spaces equipped with weighted graphs and proves uniform convergence of iterates to a unique fixed point with explicit complexity bounds.
motivation: Fixed-point theory for contraction-type mappings on generalized metric spaces with graph structures extends classical Banach/Rakotch results to broader settings, motivated by applications to integral equations and digraph problems.
method: The authors define graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings, then use iterative convergence arguments under a relaxed triangle inequality to establish existence, uniqueness, and rate bounds tied to a graph invariant.
result: They prove uniform convergence of successive iterates from any starting point to a unique common fixed point, derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound, and obtain a geometric convergence rate whose constant is the graph invariant.
conclusion: The theory is illustrated on an explicit real graded contraction attaining an interior optimum, a quadratic integral equation, and finite weighted digraphs, demonstrating the generality of the framework.

title: On The Dynamics Of Weighted Shifts On Fr\'echet Sequence Spaces Over Trees
authors: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH].
tldr: Characterizes several notions of chaos (Li-Yorke, mean Li-Yorke, distributional) for weighted backward shift operators acting on Fréchet sequence spaces built over directed trees, with corollaries for Köthe spaces and classical Banach spaces.
motivation: Weighted shift operators on sequence spaces are canonical models for linear dynamics, and extending chaos characterizations from Banach to general Fréchet/tree-indexed settings fills a gap in the linear dynamics literature.
method: Functional-analytic arguments establishing necessary and sufficient conditions on the weight sequences for each chaos property, specialized to Köthe spaces associated with directed trees and then to l^p-type Banach spaces.
result: Explicit criteria for Li-Yorke, mean Li-Yorke, and distributional chaos are obtained in the general Fréchet/tree framework, yielding concrete conditions for the classical l^p spaces.
conclusion: The work provides a unified characterization of chaotic behavior for weighted backward shifts in a broad topological-vector-space setting, generalizing known Banach-space results.

title: Consistency Considerations For Rare-event Importance Sampling
authors: Jason Beh, Emilien Flayac, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability [MATH] by importance sampling with auxiliary density [MATH], where [MATH] is drawn according to some density [MATH]. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities [MATH] and [MATH] and the set [MATH] may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime [MATH] which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case [MATH] with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.
tldr: The paper establishes consistency conditions and minimal sample-size requirements for rare-event importance sampling estimators in triangular schemes.
motivation: Rare-event probability estimation via importance sampling requires understanding when the estimator remains consistent as dimension and target sets evolve, a setting not fully covered by prior work.
method: The authors derive a necessary and sufficient condition for consistency of importance sampling estimators and analyze the hyperplane case with Gaussian densities.
result: They refine Chatterjee and Diaconis's results by giving the exact minimal sample size for consistency and show that optimal importance sampling can improve consistency in the Gaussian hyperplane case, though Monte Carlo may converge faster when both converge.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical consistency guarantees and sample-size bounds for rare-event importance sampling, with implications for choosing between importance sampling and standard Monte Carlo.

title: Statistical Geometry Of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation
authors: Quentin Berthet, Peter Bartlett, Romuald Elie, Yu-Han Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study variational inference in the presence of distributional symmetry, focusing on the interaction between two distinct group actions on a sample space: a symmetry action that leaves a reference distribution invariant, and a transport action that generates a parametric variational family by pushforward. By analyzing the algebraic structure of the total transformation group generated by both actions and the induced adjoint representation of the symmetry group on the transport Lie algebra, we establish that the Riemannian gradient of the Kullback--Leibler divergence at the true transport parameter is constrained to lie in the trivial representation of the symmetry group. Consequently, symmetry forces the gradient to vanish along all non-trivial representations. Combining this representation-theoretic constraint with parameter identifiability yields an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into three interpretable subspaces: an identifiability kernel (along which the objective is locally constant), a bias subspace (where the gradient may be nonzero due to model misspecification), and a symmetry-breaking subspace (where the gradient is forced to vanish by symmetry alone). Finally, we characterize the residual bias directions in terms of distributional mismatch between the base model and the standardized target, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition that eliminates this bias, extending the location-scale results of (Margossian and Saul, 2025) to general Lie group transformation families.
tldr: The paper analyzes variational inference under distributional symmetry using group actions and representation theory, deriving a decomposition of the transport Lie algebra and a Stein-type bias-correction condition.
motivation: It aims to understand how symmetry and transport group actions interact in parametric variational families, particularly how symmetry constrains gradients of the KL divergence and induces bias.
method: The authors study the total transformation group generated by a symmetry action and a transport action, use the adjoint representation on the transport Lie algebra, and combine representation-theoretic constraints with parameter identifiability.
result: They obtain an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into identifiability-kernel, bias, and symmetry-breaking subspaces, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition to eliminate residual bias directions.
conclusion: The work extends location-scale symmetry results to general Lie group transformation families and provides a geometric framework for bias analysis in symmetry-aware variational inference.

title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach To Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking With Nonlinear Shared Constraints
authors: Tatiana Tatarenko, Puya Latafat, Alberto Bemporad
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate [MATH] under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to [MATH] under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate [MATH].
