abstract: ArXiv:2611.10436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time [MATH] bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time [MATH] bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.
tldr: The paper develops high-order, long-time stable scalar auxiliary variable correction schemes for forced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions.
motivation: The authors aim to construct robust time-stepping methods that remain stable over long times without restrictive step-size or step-ratio constraints, for a broad class of linear predictors.
method: Two SAV correction steps are applied to any linear predictor satisfying stated order and regularity assumptions; the schemes use damped shifted kinetic-energy and higher-energy auxiliary variables with BDF time discretization.
result: The schemes yield uniform-in-time bounds and weighted dissipation estimates in two and three dimensions, with second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence observed numerically and efficient adaptive time stepping.
conclusion: The proposed corrections provide a general framework for long-time stable high-order integration of forced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, independent of the specific predictor form.

title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner For Parametric Helmholtz Problems
authors: An Ping, Zhichao Peng, Pengliang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.
tldr: The paper develops a domain-decomposed multispace reduced basis preconditioner for efficiently solving parametric Helmholtz problems.
motivation: Repeated solves of parametric Helmholtz systems are expensive, and existing MSRB preconditioners require large memory for global iteration-dependent bases.
method: The authors introduce DD-MSRB, combining trajectory-aware reduced basis training with problem-adapted spatial domain decomposition and greedy local basis selection under a global error budget, switching to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner when needed.
result: Numerical experiments on 2D and 3D Helmholtz problems show significant acceleration and memory savings, with the largest 11-million-unknown waveguide case reducing ROM storage by 44.9% and online solve time by 30.2% versus global MSRB.
conclusion: DD-MSRB provides an effective memory-efficient preconditioning strategy for parametric Helmholtz systems, but the work is purely numerical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sharp Constants And First-Order Asymptotics In A Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula For Riesz Potentials
authors: Bessem Samet Mohamed Jleli
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^\alpha\) of order \(0<\alpha<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. P\'erez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(\alpha\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.
tldr: The paper studies sharp constants and first-order asymptotics for a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu-type pointwise inequality involving Riesz potentials and a nonlinear fractional differential operator.
motivation: The work aims to determine optimal constants and refine known asymptotic convergence results for a fractional Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula in dimensions n >= 2.
method: The authors combine geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement to establish sharp constants and asymptotic corrections.
result: For n >= 3 they find the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and show it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions; in n = 2 they derive leading-order asymptotics and an explicit radial formula, plus an almost-everywhere convergence refinement.
conclusion: The paper advances the mathematical analysis of Riesz-potential Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formulas, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Limits Of Information-Flow Control Enforcement For Agentic Systems
authors: Jonathan Gregory, Kyle Domico, Kunyang Li, Jean-Charles Noirot Ferrand, Patrick Mcdaniel
abstract: ArXiv:2611.10395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Information-flow control (IFC) is a promising approach to enforce policy in agentic AI systems. However, IFC suffers from label creep, a phenomenon where monotonically increasing security labels propagate through a system and progressively limit its utility. Label creep in agentic AI systems can be mitigated using two major strategies: (1) improved system design and (2) label declassification. In this paper, we characterize how far system design alone can mitigate label creep in agentic systems. Specifically, we measure how system topology, scale, and agent composition affect utility loss and security enforcement cost proxies for conservative IFC enforcement in a stateful agentic system simulator. We develop a pipeline to systematically vary these features and measure their impacts on label propagation. Our results demonstrate strong associations between structural graph features and our IFC utility loss metric (up to a Spearman correlation [MATH] of [MATH]) and show that system size and tool allocation substantially affect how labels propagate. These findings identify design choices to reduce IFC utility loss, but they also demonstrate that system design alone cannot fully prevent utility loss due to monotonic label propagation. This motivates the development of label declassification mechanisms that aid these design choices and diminish IFC utility cost.
tldr: The paper studies how system design choices in agentic AI systems affect utility loss and security cost under information-flow control, finding that design alone cannot eliminate label creep.
motivation: Information-flow control can enforce policies in agentic AI systems but suffers from label creep, where monotonically increasing security labels reduce utility; the authors ask how much system design can mitigate this.
method: The authors build a stateful agentic system simulator and vary topology, scale, and agent composition to measure label propagation, utility loss, and security enforcement cost proxies under conservative IFC.
result: Structural graph features correlate strongly with IFC utility loss, and system size and tool allocation substantially affect label propagation, but design alone cannot fully prevent utility loss from monotonic labeling.
conclusion: Improved system design helps reduce IFC utility loss, but label declassification mechanisms are needed alongside design choices to make IFC practical for agentic AI systems.
